File chooser contract: files.choose

Status: draft, version 0.1.0, for review before any code. Nothing here is served yet.

MixOS has one system file chooser. A person picks files or a save location in it; it never opens, reads or writes the files. It is reached two ways:

  • Over the Bus, with files.choose. Apps and agents call it directly; an agent uses it to ask a person to pick a file.
  • Over D-Bus, through org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser, which portald serves and forwards to files.choose. Every app that asks the desktop portal for a dialog uses this route, whatever its toolkit (rfd, GTK, Qt, Electron and Firefox).
app --D-Bus FileChooser.OpenFile--> portald --Bus files.choose--> chooser window
agent --Bus files.choose--------------------------^                  |
          <---- outcome on the files.chosen topic, or files.choose.result

Provider

The Bus service files is served by DOpus in chooser mode, dopus --choose-service, a session unit started with the desk. It has no main window. Each accepted files.choose opens one chooser window: a single DOpus pane with Places, a path bar, a file-name field when saving, a filter menu, the caller's choices, and Accept and Cancel. Several requests open several windows. Requests keep no state from one to the next, apart from the Places, bookmarks and recent folders that the file manager also uses.

Commands

Owner dopus. They enter docs/docs/spec/bus/commands.conf.mix (status draft; classes as given below) with the code that serves them, because DOpus's registry test requires the registry to list exactly what DOpus serves.

files.choose (intent)

Opens a chooser and answers straight away; the person's answer comes later (see Outcome). Body:

FieldTypeDefaultMeaning
modeopen, save or save_filesopenWhat the person is choosing.
titlestring, 1 to 256 bytesby modeThe window title.
accept_labelstring, 1 to 64 bytesby modeThe Accept button's label. Mnemonic underscores are removed.
multipleboolfalseopen only: more than one entry may be chosen.
directoryboolfalseopen only: choose folders, not files.
filterslist of filter, at most 64noneSee Filters.
current_filterfilterfirst filterThe filter selected at first. It need not be in filters.
choiceslist of choice, at most 16noneSee Choices.
current_folderlocationlast folder used, else homeThe folder shown first.
current_namestring, 1 to 255 bytes, no /nonesave only: the suggested file name.
current_filelocationnonesave only: an existing file to save over; its folder and name are shown. Takes precedence over current_folder and current_name.
fileslist of string, 1 to 1,000nonesave_files only, and required: the names of the files about to be saved into the chosen folder.
parent_windowstring""The window the chooser belongs to. See Placement.
token1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _generatedNames the request; see below.

A location is either an absolute path written as a UTF-8 string, or a file:// URI (RFC 8089) whose percent-encoding carries the exact bytes of a path that is not UTF-8. Nothing else is accepted.

Unknown fields are ignored. A known field of the wrong type or out of range, a field used in the wrong mode, or save_files without files is refused with ARGUMENT.

Reply, rc 0:

{"request": "c42_open_1", "topic": "files.chosen"}

request is <caller>_<token>, where <caller> is the broker's connection number for the caller. A token the caller has already used for a request that is still open is refused with ARGUMENT; a caller who wants to know the request name before calling (to subscribe first, for example) sends its own token.

BUSY is returned when 8 choosers are already open on the desk, or 2 for this caller's connection. UNAVAILABLE is returned when the chooser window cannot be opened (no display, for example). Neither opens a window.

files.choose.result (query)

Body {request}. Answers with the request's state:

  • {state: "open"}: the person has not answered;
  • {state: "done", outcome: {...}}: the outcome, exactly as published;
  • ARGUMENT when the request is unknown, or its outcome has expired.

An outcome is kept for 10 minutes after it is decided, then removed. Reading it does not remove it. This command is for a caller that missed the publication; a caller that is subscribed has no need of it.

files.choose.cancel (intent)

Body {request}. Closes an open chooser. The outcome is response 1 with reason: "caller". A request that is already done is left as it is and answers rc 0. An unknown request is ARGUMENT.

files.choose.list (query)

Body none. Answers {requests: [{request, mode, title, caller, opened_ms}]} for every open chooser, oldest first.

Outcome

When a request ends, one outcome is published once on topic files.chosen and kept for files.choose.result:

{
  "request": "c42_open_1",
  "response": 0,
  "uris": ["file:///home/user/Pictures/beach.png"],
  "current_filter": {"name": "Images", "patterns": ["*.png", "*.jpg"], "mime_types": []},
  "choices": {"encoding": "utf8", "reencode": "true"},
  "reason": "chosen"
}
responsereasonWhen
0chosenThe person accepted.
1cancelledThe person pressed Cancel or Escape, or closed the window.
1callerfiles.choose.cancel, or the caller's broker connection closed.
2failedThe chooser failed after it opened. message says why.

Response codes are the portal's, so portald passes them on unchanged.

  • uris are file:// URIs, percent-encoded from the exact bytes of each path. On open, there is one unless multiple is set, never none. On save, there is exactly one. On save_files, there is one per name in files, in the same order. Each one is inside the chosen folder, with the person's answer to any name that already exists there.
  • current_filter is the filter selected when the person accepted; it is absent when there were no filters.
  • choices maps each choice's id to the option chosen; a choice with no options has "true" or "false".
  • uris, current_filter and choices are present only when response is 0.

The topic is published by files alone. Every subscriber sees every outcome; the Bus is open (docs/docs/decisions/2026-10-26-open-bus-for-agents.md), and an outcome carries paths, never file contents.

Filters

A filter is {name, patterns, mime_types}: a label of 1 to 128 bytes, and together 1 to 64 entries in two lists of strings:

  • patterns: shell globs (*, ?, [...]), matched against the file name, case sensitive;
  • mime_types: MIME types or type/*, matched by the type the shared MIME database gives the file.

Folders are always shown, so the person can move between them. When save is used with a filter whose only pattern is *.ext, a typed name without an extension gets that one.

Choices

A choice is {id, label, options, default}:

  • id and label are strings of 1 to 64 and 1 to 128 bytes;
  • options is a list of up to 32 {id, label}. When it is empty the choice is a check box, and default is "true" or "false";
  • default is one of the option ids; it is the first option when absent.

They are shown under the file list, in order.

Behaviour

  • No timeout. A chooser waits for the person as long as it takes.
  • Save. When the chosen file exists, the person confirms replacing it before Accept succeeds. save_files does the same once for all the names that exist. The chooser never creates, truncates or replaces anything; the caller does that with the URIs it receives.
  • Who is asking. When the caller is not portald, the window says which caller asked (citizen::caller_key), so a person can tell an agent's request from an app's.
  • Drive. Each chooser window answers the toolkit drive commands (docs/docs/drive.md), so it can be tested and answered over the Bus. The drive command names for several windows in one process are not yet settled (open question 2), so none are registered yet.
  • Caller leaves. When the caller's broker connection closes, its open choosers close with response 1, reason: "caller".
  • Provider stops. If files stops, every open request is lost. A caller that sees the service unregister treats its open requests as response 2.

Placement

parent_window is the portal's window identifier: "", wayland:<handle> (an exported xdg-foreign handle) or x11:<hex id>. In this version the chooser opens centred on the output of the parent window when compd can resolve the identifier, otherwise on the focused output, and stays above the parent. It is not modal to the parent; that needs xdg-foreign import and xdg-dialog-v1 support in compd, a later step.

D-Bus: org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser

portald serves the interface at version 4 on the object it already serves (see ../portal/README.md), for trusted unsandboxed callers in the session. OpenFile(s parent_window, s title, a{sv} options) -> o, SaveFile with the same arguments, and SaveFiles with the same arguments all return a Request object straight away, at /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop/request/<sender>/<handle_token>, built as for ScreenCast. Then portald calls files.choose with the mapped body and token set to the handle token.

Portalfiles.choose
method OpenFile / SaveFile / SaveFilesmode open / save / save_files
parent_window argumentparent_window
title argumenttitle (the mode's default when empty)
handle_token (s)token
accept_label (s)accept_label
modal (b)ignored: not modal in this version
multiple (b)multiple
directory (b)directory
filters (a(sa(us)))filters: kind 0 to patterns, kind 1 to mime_types
current_filter ((sa(us)))current_filter, mapped the same way
choices (a(ssa(ss)s))choices: (id, label, [(id, label)], default)
current_name (s)current_name
current_folder (ay, NUL-terminated)current_folder as a percent-encoded file:// URI
current_file (ay, NUL-terminated)current_file as a percent-encoded file:// URI
files (aay, SaveFiles)files; a name that is not UTF-8 makes the call fail with InvalidArgument

Other options are ignored. A known option with the wrong type is refused at the call with org.freedesktop.portal.Error.InvalidArgument, and no Request is created.

The outcome becomes Response(u response, a{sv} results), addressed to the Request's owner alone:

OutcomeResponse
00, with uris (as), choices (a(ss)) when the call had choices, current_filter ((sa(us))) when it had filters
11, {}
2, or files.choose refused (BUSY, UNAVAILABLE, any error), or files not registered, or lost2, {}

The Request lifecycle:

  • Request.Close() from the owner calls files.choose.cancel, removes the Request and sends no Response. Close from anyone else is refused with org.freedesktop.portal.Error.NotAllowed.
  • When the owner leaves the session bus, portald cancels its requests.
  • When portald loses the Bus or files unregisters, every open Request ends with Response 2. A Request is never left without an end: an app waiting on it must be able to tell failure from cancel.
  • Only one end wins. A Response is sent at most once, and never after Close.
  • portald subscribes to files.chosen before its first files.choose, and reads files.choose.result for each open request after it reconnects to the Bus.

Acceptance

  1. Over the Bus alone, under a nested compd: open, save (with replace confirmation) and save_files, each accepted, cancelled by the person, cancelled by the caller, and with the caller's connection dropped. Filters and choices round-trip. A path that is not UTF-8 round-trips as a URI.
  2. Over D-Bus, with a persistent zbus caller fixture (a one-shot gdbus call disconnects before the Response): each method, Request.Close (no Response), the owner disconnecting, files absent (Response 2) and Close from another sender (refused).
  3. A craft app built with rfd 0.17, on VT3: File > Open and File > Save As show the chooser; the file is opened and saved; Cancel leaves the app as it was.

Open questions

  1. FileChooser version: check the version and options against the current upstream interface XML before portald serves it.
  2. Drive command names when one process has several chooser windows: a window argument on files.ui.*, or one Bus service per window.
  3. Whether MixOS's own apps (Email's Attach files) move from the in-process toolkit::file_chooser to files.choose, keeping the toolkit chooser only for when the Bus or files is absent.
